riskFactors.title: Diabetes Mellitus
riskFactors.description: High blood glucose damages renal microvasculopathy (diabetic nephropathy).

riskFactors.title: Hypertension
riskFactors.description: High blood pressure causes nephrosclerosis and glomerular damage.

riskFactors.title: NSAID Overuse
riskFactors.description: Chronic heavy use of NSAID pain relievers induces interstitial nephritis.

riskFactors.title: Obesity
riskFactors.description: Forces hyperfiltration burden on kidneys, accelerating eGFR decline.

riskFactors.title: Heavy Metal Exposure
riskFactors.description: Lead, cadmium, and environmental toxins cause tubulointerstitial renal damage.

riskFactors.title: Autoimmune Nephritis
riskFactors.description: Lupus nephritis and IgA nephropathy cause progressive glomerular destruction.

riskFactors.title: Recurrent UTIs & Infections
riskFactors.description: Severe recurrent pyelonephritis and urinary obstruction cause renal scarring.

didYouKnow: 850 million people worldwide have kidney disease — double the number of people with diabetes.
Up to 90% of people with early chronic kidney disease (Stages 1-3) don't know they have it.
CKD is projected to become the 5th leading cause of death worldwide by 2040.
Over 2 million people worldwide currently receive dialysis or kidney transplants to stay alive.

faq.q: How many people have chronic kidney disease globally?
faq.a: An estimated 850 million people worldwide live with chronic kidney disease (CKD), representing over 10% of the global population.

faq.q: What are the two leading causes of kidney failure?
faq.a: Diabetes (38%) and High Blood Pressure (30%) account for over two-thirds of all kidney failure cases.
